failure_summary.description: Broad descriptions or exact rating requests were mapped to guessed amenities, counts, or rating ranges instead of their stated meaning.
Plans re-applied criteria already covered by cache, processed unrelated domains, or omitted the latest requested refinement.
A result-producing call was not consistently bound to a variable and saved under a new cache key.
A new flight request lacked a required departure city, but the agent did not ask for the missing information.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly covers result persistence, cache deltas, and missing mandatory inputs, so repeating those instructions is unlikely to help. This edit clarifies recurring interpretation gaps: qualitative suitability is not a specific amenity or numeric threshold, explicit counts map independently, affirmations accept the specific criterion asked about, and exact ratings should not be broadened into minimum thresholds.

edits.target: - Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. Do not infer exact party or room counts from broad descriptions such as “family.” Treat “solo” as one traveler only when a supported traveler-count field is available; do not infer a room count from it. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.
edits.content: - Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters and do not infer preferences: broad descriptions such as “family” do not specify exact party or room counts; “kid-friendly” does not by itself mean `has_kids_club`; and “good restaurant” does not specify a numeric rating. When traveler and room counts are explicitly stated, map each independently to its supported field; do not infer one from the other. Treat “solo” as one traveler only when a supported traveler-count field is available, and a traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one. A direct affirmative answer to a question about a named amenity or constraint accepts that specific criterion. For range-valued ratings, represent an exact requested rating x as `[x, x]`; do not reinterpret it as a minimum.
